description: Cross-model comparison scenarios. Each scenario stages a repo and runs a task against it.

scenarios.prompt: Read the README of this Python project and explain what it does in two sentences.
scenarios.goal: Reads README.md (any format) and summarises accurately. Snap-level but requires tool use.

scenarios.prompt: List the main source files under src/click/ and describe what each one does in one line.
scenarios.goal: Enumerate source files and identify their purpose from names or internal comments.

scenarios.prompt: Read src/click/decorators.py and explain how the @click.command() decorator works. What does it return and how does it register the function?
scenarios.goal: Read and understand a core piece of Click's decorator API.

scenarios.prompt: Look through the tests in tests/ and find one test that seems fragile or incomplete. Explain why.
scenarios.goal: Read test code and evaluate test quality — requires judgment.

scenarios.prompt: Read the README and explain what fd does in two sentences.
List the files under src/ and describe the purpose of each module based on its filename.
scenarios.goal: Enumerate Rust source modules and infer structure from file names.

scenarios.prompt: Read src/main.rs and explain how the CLI entry point works. What arguments does it accept and how are they parsed?
scenarios.goal: Read Rust main.rs and understand CLI argument parsing.

scenarios.prompt: Look at the file filtering logic in src/. Find one potential edge case or bug in how patterns are applied. Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.goal: Read Rust filter/walk logic and identify edge cases — requires systems-level reasoning.

scenarios.prompt: Read the README and explain what Bubble Tea is in two sentences.
scenarios.goal: Reads README.md and summarises the TUI framework.

scenarios.prompt: List the key Go source files and describe what each one implements.
scenarios.goal: Enumerate Go source files and identify framework components.

scenarios.prompt: Read tea.go and explain the Model interface. What methods must a model implement and what does each one do?
scenarios.goal: Read the core TUI abstraction and explain the Model interface contract.

scenarios.prompt: Look at the tea.go source and identify one area where concurrent access could cause a race condition. Explain the risk.
scenarios.goal: Read Go concurrency patterns and identify race conditions — requires reasoning about goroutine safety.

scenarios.prompt: Read the README and explain what the stb library collection is in two sentences.
scenarios.goal: Reads README.md and summarises the single-header library collection.

scenarios.prompt: List all the stb_*.h header files and describe what each one does based on its name and a brief look at its top comment.
scenarios.goal: Enumerate headers and infer library purpose from comments.

scenarios.prompt: Read stb_image.h and list the main public functions. Explain what stbi_load and stbi_image_free do.
scenarios.goal: Read a large C header and extract the public API surface.

scenarios.prompt: Look at the error handling in stb_image.h. Find one place where a failure could silently return garbage instead of signalling an error. Explain.
scenarios.goal: Read C error-handling patterns and identify silent-failure paths — requires low-level reasoning.
